name: BusyContacts
description: BusyContacts is a professional Mac contact manager that brings multiple address books together with tags, smart filters, activity history, custom fields, and contact sharing.
agentUseSummary: BusyContacts cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because it is a device-local client that syncs directly with user-selected iCloud, Google, Exchange, CardDAV, and LAN services, while BusyMac documents no BusyContacts AppleScript automation or provider API and Relay Marketplace does not currently ship local-app authority.

blocked.label: Connect BusyContacts
blocked.description: Relay does not present credentials or sessions for iCloud, Google, Exchange, Fastmail, Kerio, another CardDAV server, or LAN sharing as a BusyContacts API connection.

blocked.label: Automate BusyContacts
blocked.description: BusyMac states that BusyContacts does not support AppleScript automation, and Relay cannot drive the installed app, its UI, or private local interfaces.

blocked.label: Access contact data
blocked.description: Relay does not inspect local address-book databases, contacts, activity history, app state, or third-party service sessions; request underlying service credentials; or call private BusyContacts interfaces.

blocked.label: Change contacts
blocked.description: Reading, searching, creating, editing, tagging, grouping, sharing, importing, exporting, or deleting contacts remains unavailable without a supported and separately authorized provider or device-local contract.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until BusyMac publishes a supported BusyContacts automation contract or Relay ships a separately disclosed, user-authorized local connector.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay does not silently bridge OpenClaw to the BusyContacts Mac app, local address books, or credentials and sessions for underlying contact services.
Relay does not silently bridge Hermes to the BusyContacts Mac app, local address books, or credentials and sessions for underlying contact services.

providerSetup.blocker: BusyMac describes BusyContacts as a client that syncs directly with user-selected iCloud, Google, Exchange, Fastmail, Kerio, Zimbra, macOS Server, and other CardDAV servers. The credentials, contact data, and authorization belong to those underlying services rather than to a BusyContacts cloud API, and BusyMac explicitly states that BusyContacts does not currently support AppleScript automation. Relay's current Marketplace runtime cannot truthfully expose the installed app or its local address-book authority from Railway.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request third-party contact-service credentials as BusyContacts credentials; inspect local databases or app state; automate the app UI; or show Connect. Reconsider if BusyMac publishes an official BusyContacts API or MCP contract, Relay separately reviews an underlying service such as generic CardDAV as its own provider, or Relay ships a disclosed Mac-local connector with explicit contact permissions, per-action approval, redaction, and audit.

evidence.supports: BusyMac explicitly states that BusyContacts does not currently support AppleScript automation.
BusyMac describes BusyContacts as a Mac contact manager that syncs with iCloud, Google, Exchange, other CardDAV servers, and supported address-book sharing services.
BusyMac calls BusyContacts a client app that syncs with a server and documents direct configuration for iCloud, Google, Exchange, Fastmail, Kerio, Zimbra, macOS Server, and other CardDAV services.
BusyMac states that contact data remains on the device or on user-selected third-party sync services such as iCloud, Google, and Microsoft, which are responsible for their own storage and handling.
BusyMac documents provider-specific boundaries: BusyContacts tags map to Apple Contacts and iCloud groups, while Google proprietary labels do not synchronize through CardDAV.
BusyMac explains that users choose the underlying cloud or self-hosted sync service and that Google contact synchronization uses CardDAV.
